1247: the War of the Thuringian Succession opens. The page dates the war 1247-1264: 'Meissen acquires most of Thuringia'.

1264: Henry III asserts himself in the Landgraviate of Thuringia. 'Henry III asserts himself in the Landgraviate of Thuringia'; the Landgraviate page: 'Henry III of Meissen gained the bulk of Thuringia in 1264'.
1264: Meissen gains the bulk of Thuringia from the Ludowingian heritage, the rest becoming the Landgraviate of Hesse.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The Meissen page has no area or capital and no dates for the Milceni's later status or Merseburg and Zeitz after 983; Cliopatria's Electorate of Saxony (1363..) overlaps this dossier's last 60 years (eu-09). Not settled: the true border (all circles), who held Merseburg and Zeitz after 983 (they were recovered, undated), Lusatia (Lower and Upper) beyond the Milceni circle, the Burgraviate of Meissen (1068, 1426 or 1298), the pledge of the Pleissenland, and the Hessian part of the Ludowingian heritage. The Great Slav Rising rebels are not named on the page. Counterparts needing dossiers: March of Gero (Marca Geronis), March of Merseburg and Zeitz, landgraviate-of-hesse (eu-09), duchy-of-bohemia (eu-15). Gazetteer lacks Bautzen, Zeitz, Merseburg and Altenburg (coordinates used).
